metric_notes: Word timing counts first appearance of a distinct matching reference word type; not WER. Tokenizer splits ASCII and non-ASCII runs.
Literal, normalized lexical, matching reference bigram, and word timing are separate.
Longest gaps include initial and terminal silence within the active acoustic span; internal P95 excludes boundary waits.
CPU counters are sampled per app and child PID; decode occupancy is wall time and is reported separately.
The two lighter arms targeted and achieved 1.33 injected CPU cores, but external load declined during the sequence.
The three heavy arms targeted six CPU cores, but achieved 5.061 / 3.854 / 5.081. No fixed-six-core conclusion is supported.
All cases used original-rate public audio and isolated app profiles. The microphone was never accessed.
Initial 10:33 baseline short receipts are historical relative to the adjacent 11:05/11:09 pair.
Each independent case starts a fresh app and worker. Warm-host natural dictation is a separate condition.
External builds were present on this machine. Neither the test nor this report attributes all latency differences to source code.
